memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not go about spreading slander among your people. Do not do anything that endangers your neighbour's life. I am the LORD.'" - Lev 19:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice what sits beside slander in this verse: do not do anything that endangers your neighbour's life.

God puts gossip and physical danger in the same sentence. That should make us think.

We treat talk as harmless. It is only words. We call it sharing, or concern, or keeping people informed. But God places it next to endangering a life, because words genuinely destroy people. Reputations built over decades come apart in a week. Marriages end. People leave churches and never return.

The phrase go about is telling. It describes someone moving from person to person, carrying information. Not one careless remark, but a pattern.

Scripture is relentless on this. A gossip betrays a confidence, but a trustworthy person keeps a secret (Prov 11:13). The tongue is a small part of the body, but it makes great boasts. Consider what a great forest is set on fire by a small spark (Jas 3:5).

Here is a practical test before you speak about someone. Is it true? Is it necessary? Would I say it if they were standing here? Am I telling this to help them, or to be interesting?

Most of what we would say fails at least one of those.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you treat gossip as a serious sin or a minor social habit?
2. When did you last say something about someone you would not say to them?
3. What would change if you applied those four questions this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for treating words as harmless. Guard my tongue, and make me someone who protects reputations rather than damaging them. Amen.
